analysis.title: US Autos: October Sales Preview
key_insights: DB expects October US light vehicle SAAR at 15.6m units vs ~15.5m last year, and keeps its full-year SAAR forecast at 16.0m.
DB forecasts October sales of ~1.343m units, up from ~1.326m in September and ~1.284m in October 2025.
The October 2025 comparison base was inflated by EV sales pulled forward ahead of the September 2025 expiration of the EV tax credit.
Mid-month channel checks show industry transaction prices down -0.6% MoM and -1.1% YoY, with industry incentives down -7.8% MoM and up 8.7% YoY.
Large pickup trucks show ATP up 1.3% MoM and slightly down YoY, with incentive spending up 19.9% YoY.
On a selling-day-adjusted basis, DB projects total industry sales down -9.6% MoM and up 0.8% YoY for October.
Detroit 3 share is projected at 36.4% in October vs 38.9% a year ago (-250bps), with trucks the main driver (43.2% vs 45.9%).
Japanese 3 brands are projected to gain share to 30.2% from 30.0% a year ago, and Hyundai Group to 12.0% from 11.4%.
Stellantis incentives per vehicle are $6,155 (+1.5% MoM, +19.1% YoY), the highest among the Detroit 3, at 11.8% of ATP.
Ford ATP is $55,361 (+1.9% MoM, +3.5% YoY) and GM ATP is $52,331 (-0.1% MoM, +3.2% YoY).

sector_views.rationale: DB sees SAAR roughly in line with its prior estimates and pricing relatively resilient, with lower incentives MoM but higher YoY.

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB's estimate is slightly above the ~15.5m of October 2025, and DB is in line with its prior estimates for the month.
DB maintains its full-year SAAR forecast unchanged.
Up from ~1.326m in September and ~1.284m in October 2025.
Prices are resilient, with incentives lower MoM but still higher YoY.
Incentive spending eased from September but stays above last year.

risk_factors: The prior-year sales base is distorted by the EV sales pull forward ahead of the September 2025 tax credit expiration.
Full-size pickup incentives are up 19.9% YoY, which pressures pickup pricing.
